edits.value_json: "一 is a single horizontal stroke used for the numeral ‘one.’ An oracle-bone example records it in the phrase ‘one ox.’ The concrete source of the stroke—as a direct mark or one mediated by fingers or counting rods—remains unresolved."

"Indicative: the horizontal stroke marks the abstract number one. Accounts proposing extended fingers or counting rods as an intermediary remain possible, but the concrete graphic route is unresolved. This is a whole-graph analysis, not a compound of smaller parts."

"The curated oracle-style and small-seal images each show a single horizontal stroke. They are modern redrawings of historical script styles, not artifact images, and do not establish a precise sequence of graphic changes."

"The received Shuowen account gives 一 a cosmological role as the beginning from which heaven and earth are divided and the myriad things formed. This is a Han-era interpretation, not evidence that the graph depicted heaven or earth."

"The dictionary labels 弌 an old form of 一. A proposed graphic derivation for 弌 is tentative, and no detailed transition from 弌 to 一 is established here. A separate study reports elaborated numeral spellings from the Spring and Warring States period onward, but the scan does not resolve every printed form to a distinct Unicode identity."

"The cited oracle-bone inscription has no supplied date, and a sequence of forms across periods is not established here. The concrete source of the one-line mark—direct indication, fingers, or counting rods—also remains unresolved in the consulted analysis."
"The numeral analysis is supported; the proposal that 一 originally depicted heaven or earth is not. The chronology and development of the current senses ‘a/an’ and ‘alone’ remain unresolved."

"An oracle-bone example uses 一 in the numeral phrase ‘one ox.’ The cited study describes the numeral as the smallest positive integer and discusses ordinal ‘first’ as well; these are attested uses, not proof of a hypothetical original meaning."
"Oracle-bone writing; exact date unresolved; additional senses attested in later cited textual sources"

"The oracle-bone example has no exact date. The 字源 account cites 玉篇 and 尚書 for beginning-of-number and ordinal uses, but the supplied evidence does not establish their chronology relative to the numeral attestation. Current records list ‘a/an’ and ‘alone’ without historical dating, so no semantic transition is asserted."

"一 is one horizontal stroke used to write the number one. The line is an abstract numeral mark; whether it directly marks one or reflects counting by fingers or rods remains uncertain. An oracle-bone example records it in ‘one ox.’"
